question.text: Jensen's Alpha = Rp − [Rf + β × (Rm − Rf)]. A portfolio has Rp = 20%, Rm = 12%, Rf = 6%, β = 1.2. Jensen's Alpha is:

explanation.text: The Logic: CAPM-required return = 6 + 1.2 x (12 - 6) = 6 + 7.2 = 13.2%. Jensen's Alpha = actual return - required return = 20 - 13.2 = 6.8%. The Trap: 7.2% is just the beta-scaled equity risk premium; 8.0% is raw excess (Rp - Rm) and ignores the beta adjustment. Note: Formula per NISM-XXI-B workbook (p.370): Jensen's Alpha is actual return minus the required CAPM return.
